chunks: Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa narrated from Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Abbaruri, who said:

My father Abd al-Rahim sent me to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari (may Allah be pleased with him) regarding a matter between me and him. I attended his gathering, and a group of our companions was present, discussing some traditions and what the Truthful Ones (peace be upon them) had said. Then Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman, known as al-Baghdadi, the nephew of Abu Ja'far al-Amari, arrived. When Abu Ja'far saw him, he said to the group: 'Stop, for this man who is coming is not one of you.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari, a prominent figure in Shia history
key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: Our companions, referring to the close followers of the Imams
key_terms.الصَّادِقُونَ: The Truthful Ones, referring to the Imams
key_terms.الْبَغْدَادِيُّ: Al-Baghdadi, a known title for the nephew in this context

ai.seo_question: Who was the nephew of Abu Ja'far al-Amari that was not considered one of his true companions?
ai.summary: This narrative from Tusi's *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the rigorous scrutiny applied to claimants of deputyship during the Minor and Major Ghayba periods. The host, Abu Ja'far al-Amari, distinguishes the nephew, Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, from the true companions (*Sahaba*) based on his specific disqualification, likely stemming from his false claim to the Imamate or lack of authentic lineage. This incident underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on verifying the identity and legitimacy of deputies against impostors who sought political or religious authority.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 388 - Abu Muhammad Harun Ibn Musa has narrated from Abul Qasim Husain Ibn Abdur Rahim

that Abu Abdur Rahim sent me to Abu Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Uthman Amari for something that was between me and him. I went to him as many of our scholars were present there. They were discussing some traditions from the Imams. At this, Abu Bakr Muhammad Ibn Ahmad Ibn Uthman known as Baghdadi, the nephew of Abu Ja’far Amari came. When Abu Ja’far saw him, he said: “Stop. This man who is coming is not one of you.”
